rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unjust jinn are those who associate others with God, and they become fuel for Hell.
rows.anchor: { وأما القاسطون } يعني العادلين بالله { فكانوا لجهنم حطبا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns to Meccan unbelievers: had they followed guidance, God would have sent abundant rain after seven years of drought, increasing their prosperity as a trial; this parallels 7:96.
rows.anchor: { وألو استقاموا على الطريقة } يعني طريقة الهدى { لأسقيناهم مآء غدقا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from the Quran, the Lord's reminder, leads to severe punishment without relief.
rows.anchor: { ومن يعرض عن ذكر ربه } القرآن { يسلكه عذابا صعدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mosques includes churches, synagogues, and mosques; because Jews and Christians associate partners in prayer there, believers are commanded to worship God alone.
rows.anchor: { وأن المساجد لله } يعني الكنائس والبيع والمساجد لله { فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account returns to the nine jinn: when the Prophet worshipped at Nakhlah between Mecca and Taif, they nearly crowded over him, eager and amazed to hear the Quran.
rows.anchor: { وأنه لما قام عبد الله } النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم { يدعوه } يعني يعبده في بطن نخلة بين مكة والطائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh told Muhammad that his teaching was unprecedented and had made him enemies, then offered him their protection if he would abandon it; the verse directs him to call only on his Lord.
rows.anchor: قالوا للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة: إنك جئت بأمر عظيم لم نسمع مثله قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad cannot bring people harm or guidance or protect them from harm; God alone controls these outcomes.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا أقدر على أن أدفع عنكم ضرا ولا أسوق إليكم رشدا، والله يملك ذلك كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can protect Muhammad from God and he has no refuge apart from Him; the exception is conveying God's message, which protects him from punishment for delaying their demand for it.
rows.anchor: { أحد ولن أجد من دونه ملتحدا } [آية: 22] يعني ملجأ ولا حرزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disobey God and His messenger by refusing monotheism enter Hell forever and do not die there.
rows.anchor: { ومن يعص الله ورسوله } في التوحيد فلا يؤمن { فإن له نار جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened worldly punishment means death in battle at Badr; the question about who has weaker support or fewer troops is applied to Meccans or believers, paralleling 19:75.
rows.anchor: يعني كفار مكة عند نزول العذاب ببدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing Muhammad warn of Badr, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and others mockingly asked when the punishment would arrive; God says it may be near or postponed to a distant term.
rows.anchor: قام النضر بن الحارث وغيره فقالوا: يا محمد، متى هذا الذي تعدنا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad says he does not know whether the promised worldly punishment, the killing at Badr, will come soon or at a later appointed time; amad means a term.
rows.anchor: يقول: ما أدرى أيقرب الله العذاب أو يؤخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the unseen timing of punishment and reveals it to no one, then makes an exception for messengers He approves, to whom He discloses when it will occur.
rows.anchor: { عالم الغيب } يعني غيب نزول العذاب { فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sets angels in front of and behind a prophet to guard him until Gabriel completes the revelation.
rows.anchor: ومع جبريل صلى الله عليه وسلم أعوانا من الملائكة يحفظون الأنبياء حتى يفرغ جبريل من الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God sent a prophet, Iblis would approach disguised as Gabriel; angels guarding both sides heard the devil and identified him after Gabriel finished speaking.
rows.anchor: كان إذا بعث الله عز وجل نبيا أتاه إبليس على صورة جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protection lets Muhammad know that earlier prophets were guarded and conveyed their Lord's messages just as Muhammad is guarded and conveys his.
rows.anchor: { ليعلم } الرسول { أن قد أبلغوا رسالات ربهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God encompasses what the prophets have and counts every thing, including the descent of punishment, precisely.
rows.anchor: { وأحاط بما لديهم } يعني بما عندهم { وأحصى كل شيء عددا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ankal are kinds of punishment, the blazing fire is great fire, the choking food is zaqqum, and the painful torment is severe and injurious.
rows.anchor: { إن لدينآ أنكالا وجحيما } [آية: 12] فالأنكال عقوبة من ألوان العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food that sticks in the throat is zaqqum, and the punishment is painful.
rows.anchor: { وطعاما ذا غصة } يعني بالغصة الزقوم { وعذابا أليما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth and mountains tremble from fear, and the mountains become shifting heaps of sand whose grains follow one another when moved.
rows.anchor: { يوم ترجف الأرض } يعني تحرك الأرض و { الجيال } من الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger sent to Mecca is Muhammad, born among its people and therefore slighted; he witnesses that he delivered the message, as Moses was born among Pharaoh's people and slighted too.
rows.anchor: { إنآ أرسلنآ إليكم } يا أهل مكة { رسولا } يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه ولد فيهم فازدروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath concerns the moon, the night as its darkness departs, and the morning as its light dispels night.
rows.anchor: والليل إذ أدبر } [آية: 33] يعني إذا ذهبت ظلمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is one of the seven gates of Hell, alongside Jahannam, Laza, Hutama, Sa'ir, Jaheem, and Hawiya.
rows.anchor: { إنها } إن سقر { لإحدى الكبر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is a warning for all people; each may advance in good or fall back into sin, a threat like 18:29 and 41:40.
rows.anchor: { نذيرا } يعني تذكرة { للبشر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every unbeliever is held in Hell by their sins, while the people who receive their books in their right hands are exempt from remaining there on account of their sins.
rows.anchor: { كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People in gardens ask those in the Fire what imprisoned them in Saqar; God has released monotheists from the Fire, leaving these sinners behind.
rows.anchor: فلما أخرج الله أهل التوحيد من النار، قال المؤمنون لمن بقي في النار: { ما سلككم في سقر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inmates say they did not pray or feed the poor, joined others in falsehood and denial, rejected the Day of Judgment, and continued until death.
rows.anchor: { قالوا لم نك من المصلين } [آية: 43] في الدنيا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intercession of angels and prophets will not reach these people on that Day.
rows.anchor: { فما تنفعهم شفاعة الشافعين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning was revealed about Quraysh when they turned away from the Quran; they flee its recitation like startled wild asses.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في كفار قريش حين أعرضوا، ولم يؤمنوا بالحمر الوحشية المذعورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaswara means archers; another reported explanation is a lion.
rows.anchor: { فرت من قسورة } [آية: 51] يعني الرماة وقالوا الأسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan unbelievers demanded a revealed, individual written scripture proving their idols false, God's truth, Muhammad's mission, and angelic testimony; Gabriel offered to punish them like Israel, but the Prophet disliked this, and God says they will not believe the requested books.
rows.anchor: { بل يريد كل امرىء منهم أن يؤتى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon loses its light and the sun and moon are brought together like two yoked oxen standing before all creatures at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { وخسف القمر } [آية: 8] فذهب ضوءه { وجمع } بين { الشمس والقمر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier asks where he can flee, but there is no sheltering mountain; all end at God, with no place to depart from Him.
rows.anchor: { كلا لا وزر } [آية: 11] يعني لا جبل يحرزك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wazr is a mountain that protects a fugitive, and the word is also used for mountain in Himyari speech.
rows.anchor: لا جبل يحرزك، ويسمى حمير الجبل وزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day a person is told what they sent ahead for the afterlife and what good or evil they left after death for others to follow.
rows.anchor: من خير أو شر بعد موته في ديناه، فاستن بها قوم بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is a witness against themselves because the body and limbs testify to their deeds even if they offer an excuse.
rows.anchor: فذلك قوله تبارك وتعالى: { بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة } يعني جسده وجوارحه شاهدة عليه بعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The limbs' testimony is the meaning of the statement that a person is enough as their own reckoner.
rows.anchor: { كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا } يعني شاهدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers the Quran in Muhammad's heart, recites it to him through Gabriel so he can memorize it, and commands him to follow its content.
rows.anchor: إن علينا جمعه } في قلبك يا محمد { وقرآنه } [آية: 17] حتى نقريكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel used to recite revelation while Muhammad repeated it before the angel finished, afraid he would forget; God told him to wait and then follow Gabriel's recitation.
rows.anchor: { فإذا قرأناه } يقول: فإذا تلوناه عليك يقول: إذا تلا عليك جبريل صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unnamed human is Adam: for 21,000 years, or three seventh divisions, after heaven and earth were created, no one remembered him because he did not yet exist.
rows.anchor: { هل أتى على الإنسان } يعني قد أتى على الإنسان { حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn inhabited earth, then disobeyed God and harmed one another; God sent an angel tribe called Jinn, including Iblis, whose name was al-Harith, to expel them beyond earth.
rows.anchor: ثم إنهم عصوا الله تعالى وضر بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expelled jinn were driven into darkness behind a barrier mountain where the sun sets; between it and Mount Qaf lay a year-long distance of darkness and still water.
rows.anchor: إلى الظلمة خلف الحجاب، وهو جبل تغيب الشمس خلفه، وفى أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis and his host purified earth and worshipped God; when God announced a human successor, the angels anticipated corruption and bloodshed from the jinn they had seen, not from knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: لا أنهم علموا الغيب، ولكن قالوا ما عرفوا عن الجن الذين عصوا ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent Gabriel for soil from beneath the Kaaba, the earth's surface layer; mixed with water and left until it stank, it became sticky clay on top and dark mud below.
rows.anchor: فهبط جبريل، عليه السلام، إلى الأرض فأخذ ترابا من تحت الكعبة وهو أديم الأرض

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said people made from the sticky clay were the people of the right, while those from dark mud were the people of the left.
rows.anchor: ما كان من الحر منها فهم أصحاب اليمين، وما كان من الحمأة فهم من أصحاب الشمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays ibn Abis al-Kindi and the Jewish Malik ibn al-Dayf disputed Adam's creation; Malik claimed the Torah placed it at the creation of heaven and earth, and revelation refuted him.
rows.anchor: امرأ القيس بن عابس الكتمي، ومالك بن الضيف اليهودي اختصما بين يدي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unmentioned period was 21,000 years, or three sevenths, after heaven and earth were made.
rows.anchor: { هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر } يعني واحدا وعشرين ألف سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amshaj is mixed male and female fluid: the thick white male fluid yields nerves, bones, and strength; the thin yellow female fluid yields flesh, blood, hair, and nails.
rows.anchor: ماء الرجل غليظ أبيض، فمنه العصب، والعظم، والقوة، ونطفة المرأة صفراء رقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mixed drop develops through clot and morsel into a human, made hearing and seeing after being lifeless, so that God may test him.
rows.anchor: أي جعلناه نطفة، علقة، مضغة، ثم صار إنسانا بعد ماء ودم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed people both paths, misguidance and guidance.
rows.anchor: { إنا هديناه السبيل } يعني سبيل الضلالة والهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thankful person is a monotheist who credits God with good creation; an ungrateful person denies God's oneness or assigns God's blessings to others.
rows.anchor: { إما شاكرا } أن يكون { شاكرا } يعني موحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad must patiently await God's judgment with Mecca, not respond angrily to insults or blows, and refuse the sinner and unbeliever identified as al-Walid and Abu al-Bakhtari.
rows.anchor: فاصبر لحكم ربك } يعني حتى يحكم الله بينك وبين أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Dar al-Nadwa, al-Walid offered Muhammad half his wealth to abandon his message, Abu al-Bakhtari offered him a bride, and a third man claimed to protect him; Muhammad laughed, left, and revelation followed.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم خلوا به في دار الندوة، وفيهم عمرو بن عمير بن مسعود الثقفي، فقالوا: يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The named sinner and unbeliever in the command are al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Abu al-Bakhtari ibn Hisham; the source also associates the unbeliever label with Utba ibn Rabi'a.
rows.anchor: { ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا } [آية: 24] وهو الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amr ibn Umayr al-Thaqafi offered to protect Muhammad from God's punishment; the quoted response says no one can protect him and only conveying God's messages is excepted.
rows.anchor: قل إني لن يجيرني من الله أحد ولن أجد من دونه ملتحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God at dawn means the Fajr prayer and at evening the Maghrib prayer, with three takbirs and testimony to God's oneness at each; this repudiates shirk.
rows.anchor: { واذكر اسم ربك بكرة وأصيلا } [آية: 25] يعني إذا صليت صلاة الغداة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nighttime prayer means Isha before sleep and a long night of prayer; night vigil was obligatory for the Prophet, while tahajjud was an extra devotion for him.
rows.anchor: { ومن الليل فاسجد له } يعني صلاة العشاء الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is rest and a covering that cloaks people with its darkness; night and day are two of God's favors, with daylight given for seeking a livelihood, as 2:187 says night is clothing.
rows.anchor: يعني سكنا لكم فألبسكم ظلمته على خير وشر كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven strong heavens each have a thickness of a year's journey and are separated by the same distance; 23:17 calls them seven paths, and people should fear their collapse if they disobey.
rows.anchor: { وبنينا فوقكم سبعا شدادا } [آية: 12] يعني بالسبع السموات وغلظ كل سماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blazing lamp is the sun, which provides both light and heat.
rows.anchor: { وجعلنا سراجا وهاجا } [آية: 13] يعني الشمس وحرها مضيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clouds yield copious, successive rain: winds draw water from the lowest heaven's sea of provisions, raise and join clouds, and release rain with the wind; the Hour cannot come while any water remains.
rows.anchor: { وأنزلنا من المعصرات مآء ثجاجا } [آية: 14] يعني مطرا كثيرا منصبا يتبع بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain brings forth grain, including wheat, barley, and sesame, and plants such as wild trees and grass that grow in open country and renew annually.
rows.anchor: يعني بالحبوب كل شيء يزرع ويحصد من البر والشعير والسمسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens are densely interwoven with trees.
rows.anchor: { وجنات ألفافا } [آية: 16] يعني وبساتين ملتفة بعضها إلى بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed Day of Decision is the Judgment between creatures and the fixed time for unbelievers' promised recompense, answering their question in 36:48.
rows.anchor: { إن يوم الفصل } يعني يوم القضاء هو يوم القيامة بين الخلائق { كان ميقاتا } [آية: 17]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the trumpet blast, Israfil summons decayed bones, severed veins, torn flesh, and fallen hair to assemble for renewed life and recompense.
rows.anchor: { يوم ينفخ في الصور } وذلك إن إسرافيل، عليه السلام، ينفخ فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Souls enter the horn as black or white bees, the blessed white souls descending to al-Jabiyah near Damascus and the damned black souls to Barhut in Hadramawt; each knows its own body.
rows.anchor: فتخرج أرواحهم مثل النحل سود وبيض شقي وسعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israfil gathers souls at a rock in Jerusalem, then their flight fills the space between heaven and earth and each soul returns to its body; people emerge from graves in groups, factions, and nations.
rows.anchor: فيخرج الناس من قبورهم فوجا، فذلك قوله: { فتأتون أفواجا } يعني زمرا زمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opened heaven is split into gaps like clouds dispersing after rain in a cold north wind.
rows.anchor: { وفتحت السمآء } يعني وفرجت السماء، يعني وفتقت السماء فتقطعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains are uprooted, fly between heaven and earth from fear of God, and become a mirage like water that a thirsty person cannot find.
rows.anchor: { وسيرت الجبال } يعني وانقلعت الجبال من أماكنها، فطارت بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Great Overwhelming Event is the final blast from Jerusalem, namely the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { فإذا جآءت الطآمة الكبرى } [آية: 34] يعني العظمى

rows.speaker: الهذيل
rows.claim: Hudhayl explains the feminine grammatical form by the feminine nouns for the night's darkness and the sun, citing the phrase about darkening night and bringing out its daylight.
rows.anchor: إنما صارت مؤنثة لأن ظلمة الليل والشمسفي السماء مؤنثة

rows.speaker: شاهر همذان
rows.claim: A poem attributed to Shahir of Hamadhan at Yarmuk uses the words al-sahirah and al-hafirah in a description of return after death, as lexical poetic evidence.
rows.anchor: وإنما قصرك ترب الساهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus's peace at birth refers to his first creation without a father, at death to the grave's pressure, and at resurrection to his proof against those who called him Lord.
rows.anchor: والسلام علي يوم ولدت يعنيفي الخلق الأولى من غير أب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day a person remembers evil deeds from worldly life and is repaid; everyone sees Hell, including those blind to it in this world.
rows.anchor: { يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى } [آية: 35] يعني يتذكر ما عملفي الدنيا من شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning names al-Nadr, Habib ibn Abd Yalil, Umayya ibn Khalaf, Utba and Utayba; after Mus'ab and his brother gave away their shares of a stray camel from fear of judgment, Umayya claimed he could bear their burden before his idols.
rows.anchor: فأصاب مصعب، وأبو الدوم سهمين، ثم إن مصعب ذكر مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressor is fixed in shirk, chooses worldly life over the next, does not fear God or judgment, and consumes what is forbidden; Hell is his abode.
rows.anchor: { فأما من طغى } الثابت على الشرك، وآثر الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who can sin but restrains desire for fear of standing before God on Judgment Day will have Paradise as home, as also stated in 53.
rows.anchor: { وأما من خاف مقام ربه } يقول: مقام ذلك اليوم بين يدي ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Quraysh ask when the Hour will arrive, God answers that no one in the heavens or earth knows the unseen except God, as stated in 27:65.
rows.anchor: { يسألونك } يعني كفار مكة { عن الساعة أيان مرساها } [آية: 42]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad cannot know the Hour's timing; the end of its knowledge belongs to God, as in al-A'raf.
rows.anchor: { إلى ربك منتهاهآ } [آية: 44] يقول: منتهى علم ذلك إلى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is a messenger whose task is only to warn those who fear the Hour.
rows.anchor: { إنمآ أنت منذر من يخشاها } [آية: 45] يقول: إنما أنت رسول تنذر بالساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people see the Hour, they will think they stayed amid worldly life and pleasure for only an evening from afternoon to sunset or a morning until the sun rises higher.
rows.anchor: إلا عشية } وهي مابين صلاة العصر وإلى أن تغيب الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deafening blast is a cry heard by all creatures that strikes their hearing.
rows.anchor: { فإذا جآءت الصآخة } [آية: 33] يعني الصيحة صاخت أسماع الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person flees without looking back from brother, mother, father, wife, and children because each is occupied with an overwhelming personal concern.
rows.anchor: { يوم يفر المرء من أخيه } [آية: 34] يعني لا يلتفت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some faces are bright, happy, and glad for the good and honor they receive.
rows.anchor: { وجوه يومئذ مسفرة } [آية: 38] يعني فرحة بهجة، ثم نعتها فقال: { ضاحكة مستبشرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other faces are blackened and covered by darkness; these are the unbelieving rejecters and liars.
rows.anchor: { ووجوه يومئذ عليها غبرة } [آية: 40] يعني السواد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said the entire Quran descended from the Preserved Tablet to the angelic scribes in the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, Gabriel conveyed it over twenty months, and he delivered it to the Prophet over twenty years.
rows.anchor: نزل القرآن في ليلة القدر جميعا كله من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السفرة من الملائكة في السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden or retreating bodies are five planets: Mars, Venus, Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury; they disappear by day and appear at night, moving through the sky and hiding like gazelles in their dens.
rows.anchor: وهي خمس من الكواكب، بهرام، والزهرة، وزحل، والبرجهس، يعني المشترى، وعطارد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night darkens and the dawn brightens; God swears by these signs that the Quran is the word of Gabriel, a noble messenger who taught Muhammad.
rows.anchor: { والليل إذا عسعس } [آية: 17] يعني إذا أظلم { والصبح إذا تنفس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noble messenger is Gabriel, strong in force and honored with the Lord of the Throne.
rows.anchor: { إنه لقول رسول كريم } [آية: 19] على الله، يعني جبريل، عليه السلام، هو علم محمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Iblis asked who would confront the new prophet from Tihama, the demon al-Abyad volunteered; after Muhammad left Safa, al-Abyad took Gabriel's form, but Gabriel knocked him from Mecca to far-off India.
rows.anchor: فأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فوجده في بيت الصفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel is well-placed with God and obeyed in heaven; the word thamma means there, as in 76:20.
rows.anchor: { مطاع ثم } يعني هنالك في السماوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During the night journey, Gabriel led Muhammad among the angels, who rejoiced and greeted him; Muhammad saw Abraham and Moses and Malik, keeper of Hell, who had never spoken and showed no pity to Hell's inmates.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة عرج به إلى السماوات رأى إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم وموسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Muhammad's request Malik opened a Hell gate only as wide as a bull's nostril; its terrifying roar made the Prophet fear the Hour, so he asked Gabriel to have it shut and Malik obeyed.
rows.anchor: فكشف عن مثل منخر الثور منها، فتخلخلت فجاءت بأمر عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When night darkens, its darkness covers every animal, including beetles, snakes, scorpions, predators, and wild beasts.
rows.anchor: أظلم عن كل دابة، الخنافس، والحيات، والعقارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twilight is the light remaining after sunset until it disappears; night brings darkness, and the moon reaches fullness on nights thirteen, fourteen, and fifteen.
rows.anchor: فأما الشفق فهو الضوء الذي يكون بعد غروب الشمس إلى أن تغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's light accumulates and strengthens over three nights beginning on the thirteenth.
rows.anchor: { والقمر إذا اتسق } [آية: 18] في ليلة ثلاث عشرة، وأربع عشرة، وخمس عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People pass through successive states: semen, clot, morsel, a lifeless fetus, ensouled living person, infant, maturity, old age, death, burial, dust, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: يقول: حالا بعد حال يقول: خلقا من نطفة، ثم صارت النطفة علقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muhammad recited 96:19 and prostrated, believers followed but Quraysh clapped and whistled, mocked rather than prostrating, and disturbed Quran recitation; their worship at the Kaaba was only clapping and whistling, as in 8:35.
rows.anchor: فسجد وسجد المؤمنون معه، وكانت قريش يصفقون فوق رءوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the sins unbelievers gather; Meccans face painful punishment, except those who believe and do good, whose reward is never cut off.
rows.anchor: يكذبون والله أعلم بما يوعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn is the morning of Eid al-Adha and the ten nights are the nights before it, counted as nine days and ten nights.
rows.anchor: { والفجر } [آية: 1] يعني غداة يوم النحر { وليال عشر } [آية: 2] فهي عشر ليال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pair is Adam and Eve, the odd is God, and the approaching night is the eve of Eid al-Adha; God swears by these and by Himself.
rows.anchor: { والشفع والوتر } [آية: 3] وأما الشفع فهو آدم وحواء، عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath suffices for a rational person to recognize its greatness; God then swears that He watches over all, as in 89:14.
rows.anchor: { هل في ذلك قسم لذى حجر } [آية: 5] يعني إن في ذلك القسم كفاية لذى اللب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aad are Hud's people, named after an ancestor; Iram is one of their tribes, and its tall members resembled desert columns, reportedly eighteen or twelve cubits high, unlike any other people.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر قبيلة من قوم عاد، فقال: { إرم } وهي قبيلة من قبائلهم اسمها إرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud are Salih's people; they hollowed out the largest mountains into houses with stone doors and locks, as also described in 26:149.
rows.anchor: { الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh was named Mus'ab ibn Jabr, while another says al-Walid ibn Mus'ab; his stakes were four posts used to torture the believing hairdresser after she professed the God of Moses.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر فرعون واسمه مصعب بن جبر، ويقال: الوليد بن مصعب، فقال: { وفرعون ذى الأوتاد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter Hayjal praised God when her comb fell; after identifying the God of Moses, Pharaoh tortured her with snakes and scorpions until she melted like lead.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنها كانت تمشط هيجل بنت فرعون، فوقع المشط من يدها، فقالت: باسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is brought from a distance of 500 years with 70,000 reins and 70,000 angels on each; their fearsome eyes, fiery mouths, mountain-sized maces, and seven snake-like heads show its rage against creatures.
rows.anchor: { وجيء يومئذ بجهنم } يجاء بها من مسيرة خمس مائة عام عليها سبعون ألف زمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels restrain Hell from the creatures until it is set upright before them.
rows.anchor: متعلقون بها يحبسونها عن الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who remembers at sight of Hell is identified as Umayya ibn Khalaf; his late remembrance cannot help after he denied in worldly life, and he wishes he had prepared for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: { يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان } يعني أمية بن خلف الجمحي إذا عاين النار والملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can inflict punishment like God's punishment, whose authority is supreme.
rows.anchor: { فيومئذ لا يعذب عذابه } أي لا يعذب كعذاب الله { أحد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can bind or restrain as God binds and restrains.
rows.anchor: { ولا يوثق وثاقه أحد } [آية: 26] يعني ولا يوثق كوثاق الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is Mecca; God made it lawful for Muhammad alone for one hour, for neither earlier nor later people could kill there, except the Prophet's killing of Muqays ibn Dhibaba and another man during its conquest.
rows.anchor: { لا أقسم بهذا البلد } [آية: 1] يعني مكة { وأنت حل بهذا البلد } [آية: 2] يعني لم أحلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent and offspring are Adam and his descendants until the Hour.
rows.anchor: { ووالد وما ولد } [آية: 3] يعني آدم وذريته عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created in hardship means humans stand upright on two legs, unlike other creatures that walk on four.
rows.anchor: { لقد خلقنا الإنسان في كبد } [آية: 4] منتصبا قائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerned al-Harith ibn Amr ibn Nawfal, who asked the Prophet how to expiate a sin; when told to free a slave or feed sixty poor people, he feared his wealth would be depleted and complained to friends.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في الحارث بن عمرو بن نوفل بن عبد مناف القرشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can take away a person's safeguarded wealth, though the person boasts of having spent abundant money.
rows.anchor: { أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد } [آية: 5] يعني بالأحد الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees and counts what a person spends and will replace it for them.
rows.anchor: { أيحسب أن لم يره أحد } [آية: 7] أو يحسب هذا الإنسان أن الله تعالى ليس يرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave a person two eyes, a tongue, and two lips, and showed the two routes of good and evil.
rows.anchor: { ألم نجعل له عينين ولسانا وشفتين وهديناه النجدين } [آية: 10] يقول: بينا له سبيل الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascent is an image for sins piled like a mountain; freeing a slave or repenting and giving charity breaks them down as a mountain collapses.
rows.anchor: وهو مثل ضربه الله عز وجل له يقول: إن الذنوب بين يديك مثل الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascent means freeing a slave or feeding during famine an orphan relative or a destitute person whose back touches the earth from nakedness and need and who is too ashamed to ask; this answers the Prophet's instruction to al-Harith.
rows.anchor: { فك رقبة أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة } [آية: 14] يعني مجاعة { يتيما ذا مقربة } [آية: 15]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith means believing in God, angels, scriptures, messengers, Paradise, and Hell; believers exhort one another to persevere in Quranic duties, without which their charity and expiation are not accepted.
rows.anchor: { ثم كان من الذين آمنوا } بالله تعالى وملائكته، وكتبه ورسله وجنته وناره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Showing mercy means maintaining kinship ties and not severing them.
rows.anchor: { وتواصوا بالمرحمة } [آية: 17] يعني بالمرحمة، يعني بالرحم، فلا يقطعونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do good and exhort patience and kinship are the right-hand people who receive their books in their right hands; rejecters of the Quran's signs are the left-hand people, called so in Murad's Banu Ghutayf dialect.
rows.anchor: { أصحاب الميمنة } [آية: 18] الذين يؤتون كتبهم بأيمانهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is directed at al-Harith ibn Amr ibn Nawfal: unbelievers receive sealed Hell, while their committed torment is fixed.
rows.anchor: { والذين كفروا بآياتنا } يعني القرآن { هم أصحاب المشأمة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's forenoon is its heat; the moon follows behind it with a rustling sound in the sky; God clears daylight from night darkness and night darkness covers daylight.
rows.anchor: { والشمس وضحاها } [آية: 1] يعني وحرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath names heaven and its builder, earth and the One who spread it: God Himself.
rows.anchor: { والسمآء وما بناها } [آية: 5] يعني وبالذى بناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is Adam, fashioned by God with hands, feet, eyes, and ears; inspiring its wickedness and piety means teaching it misguidance and guidance.
rows.anchor: { ونفس وما سواها } [آية: 7] يعني أدم، وما سواها، يعني وبالذى خلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A soul succeeds when God sets it right and fails when God makes it wretched.
rows.anchor: { قد أفلح من زكاها } [آية: 9] يعني قد أسعدها الله يعني أصلحها الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud's misery twice drove denial: they disbelieved and then hamstrung Salih's she-camel; Salih had explained her water right and warned of punishment, but they rejected and killed her, so God destroyed them.
rows.anchor: { فقال لهم رسول الله ناقة الله وسقياها } [آية: 13] يعني بالرسول صالح صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by night covering day in darkness and day emerging from night; people's deeds in Mecca differ between good and evil.
rows.anchor: أقسم الله عز وجل بالليل إذا غشى ظلمته ضوء النهار، والنهار إذا تجلى عن ظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male and female are Adam and Eve; the intervening ma is extra, and God swears by Himself and these signs, as in 91:1.
rows.anchor: { وما خلق الذكر والأنثى } [آية: 3] يعني أدم وحواء وما هاهنا صلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccans' deeds vary widely between good and evil.
rows.anchor: يا أهل مكة، يقول: أعمالكم مختلفة في الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver spends wealth for God's cause, fears Him, and trusts God's promise to replace it in the afterlife with something better.
rows.anchor: { فأما من أعطى } المال في حق الله عز وجل { واتقى } [آية: 5]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage was revealed about Abu Bakr, who bought Bilal from Abu Sufyan while Bilal was tortured with a rock on his chest for his Islam, then freed him despite Abu Sufyan's taunts that his wealth was wasted.
rows.anchor: مر على أبي سفيان، وهو صخر بن حرب، وإذا هو يعذب بلالا على إسلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr answered that he hoped for forgiveness and promised to remind Abu Sufyan on the day he entered Saqar; Abu Sufyan mocked belief in resurrection and insisted the spent wealth was lost.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر، رضي الله عنه: والله، لأذكرنك هذا اليوم يا أبا سفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the generous person inclined to give again and eases that person toward good.
rows.anchor: { فسنيسره لليسرى } [آية: 7] يعني نيسره للعودة إلى أن يعطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser considers himself independent of God and denies His promise to replace giving with better; God makes it hard for him to give good.
rows.anchor: { وأما من بخل واستغنى } [آية: 8] عن الله تعالى في نفسه { وكذب بالحسنى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Sufyan's hoarded money will not help when he dies and falls into the Fire.
rows.anchor: { وما يغني عنه ماله } الذي بخل به في الدنيا { إذا تردى } [آية: 11] يعني إذا مات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides clarification of guidance and owns both worldly and afterlife life; He warns Meccans of a blazing fire that only the most wretched of them enter.
rows.anchor: { إن علينا للهدى } [آية: 12] يعني بيان الهدى { وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who denies the Quran and turns from faith is among those liable to the Fire.
rows.anchor: { الذي كذب وتولى } [آية: 16] الذين كذبوا بالقرآن وتولى يعني أعرض عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps the most God-fearing person, Abu Bakr, from Hell; his giving purifies and improves him.
rows.anchor: { وسيجنبها } يعني النار، يقول: يجنب الله النار { الأتقى } [آية: 17] يعني أبا بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second account says Abu Bakr freed Bilal after buying him from Umayya ibn Khalaf, who tortured him for Islam; Abu Bakr offered far more than the one ounce Umayya said he would have accepted, despite Abu Quhafa's objection that Bilal lacked status.
rows.anchor: مر على بلال المؤذن، وسيده أمية بن خلف الجمحي يعذبه على الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr owed no favor to the freed people and gave only to seek the face of the Most High Lord, above His creation.
rows.anchor: { وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى } يقول: يجزيه بذلك، ولكن إنما يعطى ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr would be content, having freed nine persecuted Muslims: Bilal, Amir ibn Fuhayra, his sister, Zunayra and her daughter, Haritha ibn Amr, Umm Kiyas, and al-Nahdiyya and her daughter.
rows.anchor: وأن أبا بكر، رضي الله عنه، اشترى تسعة نفر يعذبون على الإسلام، منهم بلال المؤذن، وعامر بن فهيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The morning brightness means the sun's heat at the first hour after sunrise; the night as it settles covers the day's light, and God swears by the beginnings of night and day.
rows.anchor: والضحى يعني حر الشمس وهي أول ساعة من النهار حين تطلع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel's revelation stopped for forty days, though another report says three; Meccan polytheists taunted Muhammad that God had abandoned him, while Muslims also asked about the delay.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن حبريل، عليه السلام، لم ينزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعين يوما، ويقال: ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet told those asking about revelation that Gabriel could not descend while they neglected cleaning their knuckles and trimming their nails.
rows.anchor: كيف ينزل على الوحي، وأنتم لا تنقون براجمكم، ولا تقلمون أظفاركم

rows.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
rows.claim: When Gabriel returned, Muhammad said he had longed for him; Gabriel replied that he longed more for Muhammad's honor with God but was a commanded servant, citing 19:64.
rows.anchor: أنا كنت إليك أشد شوقا لكرامتك على الله عز وجل، ولكني عبد مأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 19:64, what is before refers to worldly life, what is behind to the afterlife, and what is between them to the forty years between the two blasts; God has not forgotten Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا من الدنيا وما خلفنا من الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is better than this world; the coming afterlife will bring Muhammad repeated gifts and satisfaction.
rows.anchor: { وللآخرة } يعني الجنة { خير لك من الأولى } [آية: 4] يعني من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds Muhammad that He sheltered him as an orphan by placing him with his uncle Abu Talib, who provided for him.
rows.anchor: { ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى } [آية: 6] يقول: فضمك إلى عمك أبي طالب، فكفاك المؤنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God removed Muhammad's sin, which had weighed down his back, as also expressed in 48:1-2, where God forgives his prior and later sins.
rows.anchor: { ووضعنا عنك وزرك } [آية: 2] يقول: وحططنا عن ذنبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised Muhammad's name among people so that whenever God is mentioned, the Messenger is mentioned too, including in marriage sermons.
rows.anchor: { ورفعنا لك ذكرك } [آية: 4] في الناس علما، كلما ذكر الله تعالى ذكر معه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hardship comes with relief; the repeated definite hardship is one hardship and the two indefinite eases are two, so one hardship can never overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: إن مع الشدة الرخاء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that one hardship would never overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: لن يغلب، إن شاء الله، عسرا واحد يسرين أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After finishing the obligatory prayer and sitting before its final salutation, Muhammad should devote himself to supplication and desire his Lord; Muqatil says this forbids qunut in Fajr.
rows.anchor: والركوع والسجود، وأنت جالس قبل أن تسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that his intimate companion prayed the call and commencement twice, gave two salams, did not make qunut in Fajr, and delayed that prayer until it was quite light.
rows.anchor: عن عبدالله بن عباس، قال: فارقني خليلي على أربع خصال، كان يؤذن مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fig is the fruit, the olive produces oil, Tur Sinin is the beautiful mountain where God spoke to Moses when giving him the Torah, and every fruitless mountain is called Sinai; the secure city is Mecca, where people were safe and legal penalties were not imposed.
rows.anchor: { والتين والزيتون } [آية: 1] أقسم الله عز وجل بالتين الذي يؤكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best human form is upright walking on two legs rather than four, especially the beauty and strength of youth.
rows.anchor: { لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم } [آية: 4] يعني يمشي على رجلين وغيره يمشي على أربع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After youth and beauty, people may fall to the lowest form as their brows droop and youth, mind, strength, voice, and appearance disappear.
rows.anchor: { ثم رددناه } بعد الشباب والصورة الحسنة { أسفل سافلين } [آية: 5]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers retain an undiminished reward without reproach: good deeds from youth and health continue to be recorded in old age and illness, but an unbeliever dies in shirk and faces Hell and God's anger.
rows.anchor: { إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم أجر غير ممنون } [آية: 6] يعني غير منقوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The striking calamity is God striking His enemies; repeating the question about it emphasizes its severity, and every Quranic ma adraka informs the Prophet of the subject, unlike ma yudrika, as in 33:63.
rows.anchor: { وما أدراك ما القارعة } [آية: 3] تعظيما لها لشدتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people emerge from graves, confused and mingling like scattered moths, their numbers resemble spreading locusts, as in 54:7.
rows.anchor: يقول: إذا خرجوا من قبورهم تجول بعضهم في بعض، فشبههم بالفراش المبثوث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains become carded wool, weak and flimsy despite their former strength; their roots extend underground and their tops reach the sky.
rows.anchor: { وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش } [آية: 5] يقول: تكون الجبال يومئذ بعد القوة والشدة كالصوف المندوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy scales belong to those whose good deeds outweigh their evil deeds.
rows.anchor: { فأما من ثقلت موازينه } [آية: 6] يقول: من رجحت موازينه بحسناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only sincere monotheists make their scales heavy by saying there is no god but God; they enjoy a pleasing life in Paradise and never become dissatisfied there.
rows.anchor: ولا يثقل الميزان إلا قول: لا إله إلا الله بقلوب المخلصين في الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light scales belong to shirk: its good deeds become ash scattered by wind, leaving nothing to weigh; it is the foulest thing and the lightest in the balance.
rows.anchor: وهو الشرك لأنه لا يرى شيئا مما كسب إلا صار كالرماد، فاشتدت به الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The monotheist brings good deeds that weigh heavily, whereas the polytheist's good deeds do not count as merit and leave the scales light.
rows.anchor: فيأتي صاحب التوحيد بأعماله الصالحة فيثقل ميزانه
